summary.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 167.5 crore (up 11.9% YoY), EBITDA INR 31.3 crore (up 11% YoY, margin 18.7%) and PAT INR 21.1 crore (up 6.1% YoY, margin 12.6%). For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 two-wheeler helmet and boxes volume

financial_highlights.value: INR 3 per share on INR 5 face value (60% payout)

segments.name: STUDDS (domestic mass/core brand)
segments.commentary: Volume grew from 68.7 lakh units in FY24 to 72.6 lakh units in FY26, about 3% CAGR. Management positions it as the scale and stability base.

segments.name: SMK (premium brand)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 52% CAGR. SMK ASP rose from INR 2,359 in FY25 to INR 2,552 in FY26, and SMK sales grew about 30% YoY. Management says SMK EBITDA margin is about 10 points above STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%).

segments.name: Private label
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 22% CAGR. The largest white label, O'Neal, saw ASP rise from INR 1,831 to INR 1,918.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 20% of FY26 revenue versus 16.75% in FY25, and 22.79% in Q4 versus 17% in Q3. Management guides exports to grow 23-24% in FY27 and reach about 30% of revenue in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 17-18%, with EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels to FY26.
Q1 FY27 gross margin expected under pressure from raw material costs; margins to recover in subsequent quarters as material prices ease.

Management does not expect EBITDA margin to reach 22-23% in FY27; it expects that level only after revenue crosses INR 750 crore with operating leverage, and 12 months out margins should be better than FY26.
Advertising and marketing budget for FY27 set at INR 30 crore, across domestic and export, versus about INR 23 crore in FY26.
Normalised inventory days guided at 85-90, versus 91 days currently and 68 days in the prior year.
Expected 2-3 years of 8-9% price increases; a further 2-2.5% or 3-4% increase is possible if raw material costs stay elevated.

Capacity: installed capacity rises from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units (about 33%), with the first 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27 and the second 1.5 million over the following 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 1.5 million units targeted by Q2 FY27, with a second 1.5 million units expected over the following 15-18 months; total installed capacity to rise from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units.
Capacity utilisation FY26: two-wheeler helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 88%, water decals 57%. Q4 FY26 utilisation: helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 91%, water decals 57%.
Capacity figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix; unpainted-heavy mix raises effective capacity.
Italy subsidiary being incorporated, with a warehouse in Reggio Emilia via a third-party 3PL. Initial stock of 10,000-15,000 units, about three months' cover, with sales expected from mid-Q2 FY27.
Additional warehouse added in Faridabad in FY26.
Riding jackets and an external Bluetooth communication system for helmets are in advanced prototype; commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Price increases averaging 8-9% across the portfolio and channels from 1 April 2026, with export price increases of about 9-10%. Management says the 8-9% offsets current material costs but not full-year costs if they stay at peak levels.
Raw material prices rose after March and have eased in the last two weeks; management says they remain about 20-25% above the pre-spike level and expects about 2-3 months to return to Nov-Dec levels.
Management reports no volume or demand pressure after the April price increase, and says dealers expected a larger increase.
Unorganised share of the Indian helmet market is estimated at 25-30% (not less than 20%), expected to fall to 10-15% over 2-3 years.
Europe: Italy is the focus market, to be served dealer-direct. Mexico: a 1,200-store retail chain signed; Mexico helmet market about 2.5 million units, with the company below 1% share.
Competition: management says unorganised players may exit under price pressure, and many brands, including Chinese OEM suppliers, have raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12 million capacity target conservative if unpainted helmets are produced more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is fungible. The 12 million figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix, and capacity rises if the unpainted share increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and will 8-9% price increases offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8-9% almost offsets current material prices, but not if costs stay at peak. Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure, and recovery is expected once material prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach 22% as revenue crosses INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not in FY27 because of Q1 raw material pressure. Operating leverage is expected to lift margins above FY26 levels 12 months out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between SMK and STUDDS, and between export and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: SMK EBITDA is about 10 points higher than STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%). Export and domestic margins are roughly similar, with exports mostly SMK, and a gap of about 10 points is cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the European subsidiary moved from Spain to Italy?
qa_highlights.answer: The Spanish distributor objected to a direct subsidiary there. Italy has no direct importer, is the largest European market, and is served by a Dutch distributor with small volumes. The warehouse will be in Reggio Emilia.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from 68 to 91?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the new Faridabad warehouse and higher US inventory with rising US sales. It says 85-90 days is the comfortable range.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: prices spiked to about 150 (index) before easing to 120-125, and Q1 FY27 gross margin is expected to be under pressure.
Working capital: inventory days rose to 91 from 68, and management targets 85-90 days.
Start-up costs and margin drag from the Italy subsidiary and the Europe 3PL warehouse, and new export markets with their own homologation rules (Brazil, Indonesia, Sri Lanka).
Execution on the Decathlon non-motorised helmet supplies from July 2026 and on the 1.5 million unit capacity addition by Q2 FY27.
Marketing spend to rise to INR 30 crore in FY27, which could weigh on operating margins.
Leadership transition: Bharat Goyal becomes CFO from 1 July 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the SMK and export story, but candid that Q1 FY27 margins will be pressured by raw material costs. Management was direct on the 22% margin question and on the Spain-to-Italy change, and gave some numbers only as ballparks.
key_quotes: So, export and domestic would be quite similar because most of the exports is with SMK.
I don't think 22 %-23% is what I think will happen this year.
So, I don't see any demand pressures as of now.
We have never reduced our prices.

adds.what: 1.5 million units two-wheeler helmet/box capacity (phase 1 of 9.25M to 12M+ installed capacity)
Second 1.5 million units helmet/box capacity over following 15-18 months

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 17-18% with flat EBITDA margin (~19.3%), backed by 1.5M helmet units of capacity by Q2 FY27 (9.25M to 12M+ total, ~33%), 8-9% price increases from April 2026, and export growth of 23-24%; utilisation is high at 89% but the second 1.5M tranche is 15-18 months out and no firm order book is cited.

mgmt.note: Bharat Goyal elevated to CFO effective 1 July 2026; no stated growth plan specific to the role.
